extracted.intended_audience: program chairs, conference organizers, program committee members, and reviewers for computer science conferences (SIGPLAN/ACM)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implementation recommendations for running fair, high-quality peer review for computer science conferences, with emphasis on double-blind reviewing, author response, external review committees, conflict management, and program committee practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver expert, fair, and thoughtful reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important job of a program chair, program committee, and external review committee is to deliver expert, fair, and thoughtful reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviewers have scientific training, experience, and skills to judge contribution, novelty, correctness, and methods; provide sufficient time for evaluations; use multiple reviewers where breadth of expertise is required; program chair is responsible for delivering sufficient reviewer expertise for every submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified expert reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewing seeks to evaluate research using qualified experts, who have the scientific training, experience, and skills to judge the merit of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain three to five reviews, expose all reviews to all reviewers, and use author response and discussion (online or in person) to 'trust and verify' that reviewers make appropriate scientific judgements based on expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: With double-blind reviewing, neither authors nor reviewers are revealed. Its purpose is to focus the evaluation on the quality of the submission by reducing human biases with respect to the authors' race, gender, institution, and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-blind reduces implicit reviewer bias and, compared to single-blind, many studies show improved result quality and fairness. It is widely recommended and used by many ACM conferences and some journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind until accept
rubrics_metrics.description: I suggest double-blind until accept, such that papers that are not accepted will remain double-blinded when submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments vs 'light double-blind' noted: unblinding after first review is insufficient because later phases (author response, online discussion, PC meeting) remain susceptible to bias; program chair can unblind in rare cases if essential; authors who do not cite their own work properly should be penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response / rebuttal phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Author response gives authors a single opportunity to answer reviewer questions and correct misunderstandings before the committee decides the fate of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits: increases reviewer accountability; gets reviews finished before PC meeting; allows program chair to obtain additional reviews. Practical guidance: require reviewers to submit about a week before the PC meeting; give authors two or three days to compose a response; reviewers should read responses and adjust reviews before the meeting; discussion leader should summarize response at meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: External review committee
rubrics_metrics.description: External review committees consist of reviewers who have the same accountability and responsibilities as the program committee, but generally review fewer papers and do not travel to committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use externally selected review committees to add expertise, handle rising submission numbers, ease double-blind implementation, and improve review quality. They should follow same conflict and assignment processes, be sized to manage reviewer load, review only where they add expert value, and can be included in the author response cycle for accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission anonymization rules for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: To make your submission double-blind, do not reveal the identity of any author in the text (e.g., no author names, funding sources, or personal acknowledgments). Never put your name in the submission file name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not eliminate essential self-references; use third person when referring to prior work (e.g., 'We build on the prior work by Jones and Smith [JS 2003]'). If supplementary material reveals identity, send it to the Program Chair or note it's available from the chair upon request. Authors may post and give talks but should not email or otherwise explicitly act to bring the submission to PC members' attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact program committee during submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should not email, use social media, or otherwise explicitly act to bring their submissions to the attention of program committee members while their paper is under submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-blind is not intended to retard dissemination; authors may post or present, but direct solicitation of PC influence is prohibited as an ethical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest tracking and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission software should automate tracking and enforcing conflicts. Authors, committee members, and the program chair must enter conflicts and the chair should review conflicts for consistency and resolve inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software must ensure conflicted committee members never see reviews, rankings, or reviewers of conflicting submissions; committee members must leave the room during discussions of conflicted submissions; authors and reviewers should specify institutional and personal conflicts; historical conflict persistence helps reduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program chair authority to unblind when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers believe that double-blind is an obstacle to objectively reviewing a submission, they should contact the program chair, who has the option to unblind the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unblinding should be rare and used only when unblinded materials are essential to evaluation (e.g., access to special equipment or methods). The program chair may provide necessary information; reviewers should first appeal to the chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software support for reviewer assignment and expertise prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference software should use information retrieval techniques to predict reviewer expertise to assist reviewers with bidding and program chairs with reviewer assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mine prior reviewer publications (ACM DL and others) and score reviewers for expertise on each submission based on publication history to ease assignment and improve fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software retention of prior submissions and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The software should retain prior submissions, their reviews, author responses, and a summary of differences with the new submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make this prior material available to current reviewers after their initial review to encourage authors to incorporate prior comments and to utilize prior reviews. Advocate for ACM/SIGPLAN-wide policy to consistently give access to prior submissions and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and sequencing of reviews and author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should submit initial reviews well in advance of the program committee meeting; authors then have a short window to respond; reviewers should read responses and adjust reviews before the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical schedule suggested: reviewers submit ~1 week before meeting; authors have 2-3 days to respond; reviewer who leads discussion summarizes the response at the meeting. This sequencing improves accountability and allows time for additional reviews if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and bibliography policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Page limits on final versions seem counterproductive to encouraging research quality; some conferences now apply page limits only to main text and allow an unbounded bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage inclusive references by removing bibliography page limits; allow authors to add archival appendices in the ACM Digital Library rather than strict page-count limits for archival material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling program committee submissions and nepotism
rubrics_metrics.description: Because submitters may be program committee members, the program chair should apply practices to limit but not eliminate potential abuses from nepotism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: handle PC-member submissions in a process before or after the PC meeting; use external review committees to review PC submissions separately; monitor committee members for substantially more positive recommendations for students/colleagues; encourage reconsideration of outlier reviewers; discount scores when choosing papers for discussion; keep conflicted authors out of discussion rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and mitigate reviewer outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: To combat explicit bias against submissions, the program chair should monitor the recommendations of all reviewers and identify reviewers substantially more negative (or positive) than others or outliers on many submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair can encourage reviewers to reconsider, discount outlier scores when choosing papers for discussion, and encourage online discussion of impacted papers to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and accountability parity for external reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: External review committee members should have the same accountability and follow the same processes (conflicts, bidding, reviewing standards) as program committee members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They generally review fewer papers, do not attend the PC meeting, are selected to improve breadth/depth of expertise, can make relative judgments, and should be included in the author response cycle to ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person program committee meetings for transparency and training
rubrics_metrics.description: In-person PC meetings enable reviewer discussions to be public to the rest of the committee, encourage reviewer accountability, and support training of junior researchers and community building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings help establish and communicate scientific standards (novelty, methods), expose factions, reduce concentration of publication power, and train recent PhDs; recommended some overlap year-to-year (about 10% to 15%) to balance consistency and turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage inclusive community values and editorial transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference PC processes should promote inclusive references, shared research values, and open discussion rather than concentrating decision power in few senior researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference reviewing with rotating PC membership and open discussion promotes a larger, more diverse set of decision-makers and transparency in how standards are applied, benefiting community training and research variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits and imperfectness of double-blind
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-blind is not perfect and can be subverted, but it improves fairness and quality by focusing evaluation on submissions rather than authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize objections (identifiability via citations, perceived harm to prolific authors, loss of author learning for PC members) and mitigate them through guidance to authors, program chair oversight, and empirical study; community surveys and literature support double-blind's benefits for reducing bias.
